Scientists discover a new type of depression that common antidepressants struggle to treat

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (978 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A newly identified form of depression may help explain why some people struggle to find relief from commonly prescribed antidepressants.
  • According to recent reports, the discovery emerged from an analysis of clinical and genetic information from more than 10,000 Australians with depression.
  • According to recent reports, circadian depression is associated with the body's 24-hour internal clock, which helps regulate when we feel awake and when we feel sleepy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A newly identified form of depression may help explain why some people struggle to find relief from commonly prescribed antidepressants. Researchers at the University of Sydney have discovered a subtype called "circadian depression," which appears to be closely connected to the body's internal biological clock.

According to recent reports, the discovery emerged from an analysis of clinical and genetic information from more than 10,000 Australians with depression. Nearly one-quarter of the participants in the study, which focused on people with severe, recurrent or persistent depression, indicated characteristics of this newly identified subtype.

According to recent reports, circadian depression is associated with the body's 24-hour internal clock, which helps regulate when we feel awake and when we feel sleepy. People with this form of depression tend to respond less favorably to common serotonin-based antidepressants. However, treatments that target the brain circuits involved in controlling circadian rhythms, including melatonin, melatonin-targeted antidepressants and light therapy, may offer more effective options.

Published in the British Journal of Psychiatry, the findings shed light on the genetic factors associated with this subtype and offer a possible explanation for why widely used medications such as SSRIs (selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors) are less effective for some patients.

A Hidden Type of Depression Affecting Nearly One in Four Patients Studied.

In a recent development, to investigate the biological differences between forms of depression, researchers examined information collected through the nationwide Australian Genetics of Depression Study. Their analysis included clinical histories and genetic data from more than 10,000 people who had experienced depression.

Industry observers note that the researchers identified nearly 25 percent (2,604 participants) as having circadian depression. Several recognizable patterns distinguished these individuals from other people with depression.

Those with the circadian subtype were more likely to experience seasonal changes in their depression, sleep for longer periods when depressed, and wake up feeling exhausted despite spending more time in bed. They were also more likely to be night owls, meaning they naturally preferred staying awake late and waking later in the day.

According to recent reports, the differences extended beyond sleep patterns. Depression often began earlier in life for these individuals, and their symptoms tended to be more severe (such as mania and higher levels of suicidal thoughts). Genetic analysis also revealed an increased predisposition to inflammatory and cardiovascular health problems, along with major neurodevelopmental disorders, including ADHD.

According to recent reports, first author Dr. Emiliana Tonini from the University of Sydney's Brain and Mind Center remarked:.

"Our research has identified circadian depression as a latest subtype, affecting around a quarter of people in our study into those with severe, recurrent or persistent depression.

"Depression is not a uniform illness, and understanding the characteristics of different subtypes means that we can give people earlier access to treatments that will be most effective for them.".

Why Common Antidepressants May Be Less Effective.

One of the most key implications of the discovery involves how depression is treated.

It has been revealed that medications such as SSRIs and SNRIs (serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors) are generally among the first treatments offered to people diagnosed with depression. These drugs work by influencing chemical messengers in the brain that help regulate mood.

However, the researchers found that these medications tend to be less effective for people with circadian depression. Individuals with this subtype also experience more side effects, suggesting that conventional antidepressants may not be the best initial approach for everyone.

Industry observers note that because circadian depression is closely associated with the body's internal clock, therapies designed to influence that clock may be particularly useful. Light therapy, for example, uses controlled exposure to bright light to help regulate biological rhythms. Melatonin, a hormone involved in signaling when the body should prepare for sleep, and antidepressants that target melatonin pathways may also be relevant treatment options.

According to recent reports, co-senior author Dr. Jacob Crouse from the Brain and Mind Center explained:.

"Because circadian depression is linked to people's internal body clock, treatments targeting the circadian rhythm, such as light therapy and melatonin, may be much more relevant, and clinicians should reach for these much earlier in people with this presentation.

"For those who find that antidepressants are not working for them, it is important to speak to your clinician for advice about your individual circumstances.".

A Latest Approach Could Improve Depression Treatment in Young People.

Recognizing circadian depression earlier could be especially crucial for younger patients, who may otherwise spend valuable time trying medications that are less suited to their particular form of depression.

Professor Ian Hickie, Co-Director of the Brain and Mind Centre and a clinical psychiatrist, warned that failing to identify this subtype in young people can contribute to unsuccessful early treatments and unnecessary side effects.

The findings highlight the importance of recognizing that depression is not a single, uniform condition. Different biological mechanisms may contribute to similar symptoms, meaning that treatments effective for one person may provide much less benefit to another.

By identifying patients whose depression is closely tied to circadian rhythms, clinicians may be able to offer more targeted treatments earlier rather than relying on the same initial medication approach for everyone.

"We really want young people to receive the most appropriate treatment early in their course of illness.

"Most young people will be offered SSRIs first up, but for at least a quarter there are better circadian-focused medical and behavioral options to help treat and manage their condition.".

Materials provided by University of Sydney. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

It has been revealed that I often find it quite dull that the main takeaway far too many people have taken from Dark Souls, aside from thinking that the most interesting thing is its combat, is that it's all so bloomin' grimdark. I'm not saying I need sunshine and rainbows, I'd just like a vibe that's even remotely trying to be different from FromSoftware's seminal work. And so! I am quite pleased to discover MycoRelic, a Soulslike that pits you as a robot that covers its body in mushroom parts that offer elemental powers.

According to recent reports, mycoRelic, from the offset, has this low-poly style that almost reminds me of oldschool RuneScape in a way I clown with quite quickly. The game looks good! The vibes look odd and, thankfully, not particularly derivative of medieval aesthetics. But while I am vibes-first when it comes to games, a Soulslike does live and die by its systems, and the systems here sound quite intriguing.

Sources indicate that for starters, there are no classes to speak of, just various weapons with their own moves and stats, and armour that "suits your playstyle and aesthetic." Huzzah! A game that understands one of the best bits of Dark Souls is dressing up. When you start out, you just have a "decrepit, moldy frame," but over time you can replace parts of it to improve your health, stamina, frame integrity, and the "potency of your fungal magic." Mycellic music to my ears.

Different fungi have different powers, and can be combined to create new effects, or used in a multitude of ways; healing water can restore your friends or put out a fire for example. And oh, yes, there's co-op too, though I don't know if it's the friction-heavy Dark Souls kind or the seamless, hassle-free kind. On top of all this you've got an air-dash and can glide too, offering up some tasty platforming potential not typically found in the genre. I like it! And it just came out in 1.0 after a period of early access. If you fancy giving it a go, there's still a demo on Steam, or you can just pick up the full thing.

Britain's Marc 'Caedrel' Lamont and Dan Gaskin were among the winners at the 2026 Esports Awards in Miami, where Counter-Strike 2 was named game of the year and Team Vitality and BLAST also took industry honours. The results crown a strong Counter-Strike year eight days before the next CS2 Major begins in Singapore.

Industry observers note that the 2026 Esports Awards honoured two British figures from the streaming and broadcast side of the scene. Caedrel is a League of Legends streamer and co-streamer. Gaskin works as a caster.

Recent findings suggest that the ceremony took place on the evening of 17 November at the Adrienne Arsht Center for the Performing Arts of Miami-Dade County. It is the scene’s main end-of-season awards show. The event began in London in 2016.

At Worlds 2026, Caedrel was the top co-streamer for both hours watched and peak viewers, according to Esports Charts.

His co-stream success came in a softer year for the tournament overall. Worlds 2026 peaked at 3.98 million viewers, which was 41% lower than the previous year. Caedrel’s numbers show how much attention a single co-streamer can hold even when the event’s headline peak falls.

Gaskin was not the only caster honoured in Miami. The other broadcast honours went to Alex ‘Machine’ Richardson for Play-by-Play Caster of the Year, Iain Chambers for Host of the Year and Anthony ‘NAMELESS’ Wheeler for Analyst of the Year. iShowSpeed was named Streamer of the Year.

Counter-Strike featured prominently among the industry prizes. Vitality’s award as best organisation came alongside Esports PC Player of the Year for Mathieu ‘ZywOo’ Herbaut. OpTic Texas were named Esports Team of the Year.

BLAST, which stages many of its events in Europe, was named Esports Tournament Organiser of the Year.

Vitality’s results through the year back up their award. They beat Spirit to win IEM Rio 2026 on 19 April, giving them back-to-back ESL Grand Slam titles. ZywOo took his 31st career HLTV MVP award at that event.

"When I won this award in 2023, I never thanked my parents" 😅❤️.

Esports Colour Caster of the Year — @DanGaskin pic.twitter.com/oZBw5FItEJ.

— Esports Awards Presented by Thunderpick (@esportsawards) November 18, 2026.

Industry observers note that the team’s form held into the autumn. Vitality swept MOUZ 3-0 in the ESL Pro League Season 24 grand final on 11 October. That was their second title in a row after winning StarSeries Fall in September.

In a recent development, the PGL Major Singapore 2026 runs from 25 November to 13 December with 32 teams and a US$1,250,000 prize pool, The Kallang reported. The final stages will be played at the Singapore Indoor Stadium from 10 to 13 December.

Latest gum disease treatment kills bad bacteria while sparing the good

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1164 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, researchers in Japan have developed a promising new treatment for gum disease that kills harmful bacteria while leaving beneficial microbes unharmed.
  • Developed by scientists at Nagoya University, the treatment combines antibodies obtained from egg yolks with near-infrared light.
  • Why Conventional Gum Disease Treatments Can Cause Problems.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, researchers in Japan have developed a promising new treatment for gum disease that kills harmful bacteria while leaving beneficial microbes unharmed. Unlike conventional approaches that can eliminate both good and bad bacteria, the new therapy is designed to target specific microbes responsible for damaging gums and the bone that supports teeth.

Developed by scientists at Nagoya University, the treatment combines antibodies obtained from egg yolks with near-infrared light. Early experiments in human cell cultures and mice suggest that it could offer a more precise way to combat periodontitis, a serious form of gum disease that can eventually lead to tooth loss. The findings were published in the Journal of Translational Medicine.

Why Conventional Gum Disease Treatments Can Cause Problems.

It has been revealed that the human mouth contains a complex community of microorganisms, many of which play key roles in maintaining oral health. Problems can arise when harmful bacteria multiply and disturb this delicate balance.

In a recent development, one particularly troublesome species is Porphyromonas gingivalis (P. gingivalis), which scientists classify as a keystone pathogen. This means it can have an outsized influence on the surrounding microbial community, even when it is not especially abundant. By promoting inflammation and disrupting the normal balance of oral bacteria, it can contribute to the destruction of the bone that holds teeth in place.

In a recent development, treating periodontitis often involves eliminating the bacteria responsible for the infection. However, some existing antimicrobial treatments do not distinguish between harmful organisms and microbes that help maintain a healthy mouth.

"Current treatments for periodontitis, including antibiotics and antimicrobial photodynamic therapy (aPDT), eliminate both pathogenic and beneficial oral bacteria," noted Kazuhide Sato, one of the corresponding authors and a lecturer at Nagoya University. "These approaches often disrupt the entire oral microbial ecosystem and can also release lipopolysaccharide (LPS), an endotoxin that may exacerbate inflammation.".

Scientists Adapt Cancer Therapy to Target Gum Disease Bacteria.

To overcome these limitations, the Nagoya University team turned to a technology originally designed to treat cancer. Known as near-infrared photoimmunotherapy, it uses antibodies linked to a light-sensitive dye to recognize specific targets. Once the compound attaches to its intended target, exposure to near-infrared light activates the dye and produces a damaging effect.

Recent findings suggest that the researchers adapted this strategy to attack P. gingivalis without unnecessarily disturbing other oral bacteria. Their approach relies on IgY, a type of antibody collected from the egg yolks of hens that have been immunized against the pathogen.

Recent findings suggest that egg yolk antibodies offer a practical advantage because they can be produced in large quantities at relatively low cost. This could make them an attractive option for developing targeted treatments that are affordable and scalable.

In a recent development, the resulting technology, called near-infrared photo-antibacterial targeting therapy (NIR-PAT²), was developed by researchers at Nagoya University Graduate School of Medicine. The team included first author Hiroshi Maruyama, Professor Hideharu Hibi, and corresponding authors Sato and Kiyoshi Sakai.

To determine whether the treatment could destroy harmful bacteria while protecting healthy tissue, the researchers tested it in human cell cultures and mice. They also compared its effects with those of conventional antimicrobial therapies.

Light-Activated Antibodies Destroy Harmful Bacteria.

Laboratory experiments highlighted that the antibody and dye combination attached specifically to P. gingivalis. Other bacterial species and healthy human gum cells were left unaffected.

When the researchers illuminated the targeted bacteria with near-infrared light, the activated dye damaged their outer membranes, ultimately killing them.

Sources indicate that microscopic examination revealed an important difference between this technique and conventional antimicrobial light therapy. Bacteria exposed to the fresh treatment developed tiny openings in their membranes but largely maintained their overall shape. By contrast, conventional antimicrobial photodynamic therapy caused the bacteria to break apart completely.

Industry observers note that the distinction matters because destroying bacterial cells can release substances that contribute to inflammation. Preserving the overall structure of the targeted bacteria, even after killing them, could help limit this unwanted effect.

Recent findings suggest that the researchers also examined how the treatments affected healthy human gum cells. Their targeted therapy caused no detectable harm to these cells, while conventional antimicrobial photodynamic therapy produced cellular damage and slowed healing.

New Treatment Reduces Bone Loss in Mice.

The team next investigated whether these laboratory findings would translate into meaningful improvements in gum disease.

In mice with periodontitis, the experimental therapy significantly reduced the loss of alveolar bone, the part of the jawbone that surrounds and supports teeth. Preventing this type of bone deterioration is especially crucial because advanced periodontitis can loosen teeth and eventually cause them to fall out.

Analysis of the animals' saliva revealed another encouraging result. The treatment reduced P. gingivalis while preserving beneficial Streptococcus bacteria, helping maintain a healthier balance of microorganisms in the mouth.

Conventional antibiotics and antimicrobial photodynamic therapy, on the other hand, eliminated both harmful and beneficial bacteria in the experiments, causing broader disruption to the oral microbial community.

"Results demonstrated that, unlike antibiotics or standard light therapy, this approach selectively removes the primary pathogenic species while preserving the remainder of the oral bacterial community," Sato remarked.

Together, the findings suggest that targeting individual disease-causing bacteria could help control gum disease while avoiding some of the unintended consequences of broader antimicrobial treatments.

AI Could Help Develop More Precise Gum Disease Treatments.

Although the early results are promising, the researchers recognize that periodontitis is a complex disease involving multiple bacterial species. Eliminating P. gingivalis alone may not be sufficient to treat every case.

To address this challenge, the team plans to use artificial intelligence (AI) to examine publicly available information about oral bacteria. By identifying other crucial microorganisms and studying how different species interact, they hope to uncover additional targets for future therapies.

The researchers also see potential implications beyond oral health. Periodontitis has been linked to several other medical conditions, including rheumatoid arthritis and diabetes.

Industry observers note that understanding the relationships between oral bacteria and these conditions could eventually help scientists identify which patients are most likely to benefit from specific treatments. AI analysis may play a role in making those decisions and guiding the development of more personalized approaches to gum disease.

Sources indicate that for now, the therapy remains experimental, with its effectiveness demonstrated in laboratory studies and mice rather than human clinical trials. However, the findings point toward a possible future in which treating gum disease means selectively removing harmful bacteria instead of disrupting the entire microbial community that helps keep the mouth healthy.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, diablo 4’s segment in the big Diablo 30th Anniversary Spotlight was among the biggest, even if the reason most of us tuned in was somewhat spoiled earlier in the same livestream. Blizzard unveiled the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The first class, being the Paladin, is already available to play for anyone who pre-ordered the expansion, but the Warlock won’t be accessible until the expansion arrives in late April.

The Warlocks are positioned as the opposite of the Paladins, in that they don’t mind utilising forbidden knowledge, drawing on the powers of Hell itself to fight its own overlords. The Warlock is the edgy, antihero counterpart to the Paladin’s purity and devotion to the Light.

In a recent development, the livestream did not show off any Warlock gameplay, but Blizzard is planning a dedicated livestream to show off the new class’ gameplay, and dig deeper into its lore and abilities. That show is scheduled for March 5.

What we did get to see was our first look at Skovos, the expansion’s new region. This Mediterranean-inspired location is where the new story arc will unfold, but it’s also being positioned as the endgame destination for Diablo 4 once the credits roll.

Lord of Hatred, of course, as previously revealed, introduces two new endgame modes in War Plans, and Echoing Hatred.

It has been revealed that war Aims lets you create a custom playlist of up to five endgame activities to target specific rewards and create your own experience. There’s a fresh activity tree that works with all endgame activities, and creating War Plans is how you earn progression there.

Industry observers note that echoing Hatred, on the other hand, is a rare event that pits you against legions of Mephisto’s minions. It’s triggered through a rare lootable item that unlocks access. It’s essentially horde mode; where you’ll face unending waves of enemies, though not without a couple of twists.

Recent findings suggest that we also got a bit more colour on the expanded class skill trees, which all players will benefit from when the expansion arrives. The Talisman system, which unlocks set bonuses, was also shown off. And, of course, the return of the iconic Horadric Cube, which gives you control over Affixes.

The Anniversary Spotlight should’ve had a Year of the Warlock subtitle, because the class is also making its way to both Diablo Immortal, as well as Diablo 2: Resurrected. The showcase revealed the Reign of the Warlock DLC, which adds the aforementioned Warlock to D2R - its first newly introduced class in 25 years.

According to recent reports, reign of the Warlock, which is available now in D2R, also makes a few updates to the game, such as newly introduced quality of life features, the Colossal Ancients endgame encounter, updated Terror Zones and more. You also get some cosmetics in Diablo 4 if you purchase this expansion.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Yesterday, a rumor emerged on X claiming that Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra, the upcoming World War II-era superhero game led by Uncharted creator Amy Hennig, was being cancelled.
  • The rumor stemmed from a now-deleted X post from a fan account called Marvel 1943 Rise Of Hydra Countdown claiming, through supposed inside sources, that Skydance was preparing to announce the game’s cancellation.
  • Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was revealed in 2022 and stars Captain America and Black Panther (Azurri, T'Challa's grandfather), alongside Howling Commandos member Gabriel Jones and Wakandan Spy Network leader Nanali, as they battle Hydra during World War II.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yesterday, a rumor emerged on X claiming that Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra, the upcoming World War II-era superhero game led by Uncharted creator Amy Hennig, was being cancelled. After making the rounds on social media, upcoming reports claim this is not the case, at least for now.

The rumor stemmed from a now-deleted X post from a fan account called Marvel 1943 Rise Of Hydra Countdown claiming, through supposed inside sources, that Skydance was preparing to announce the game’s cancellation. This rumor was quickly picked up and circulated by online gaming circles, gaining steam due to growing uncertainty around the game’s status.

Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was revealed in 2022 and stars Captain America and Black Panther (Azurri, T'Challa's grandfather), alongside Howling Commandos member Gabriel Jones and Wakandan Spy Network leader Nanali, as they battle Hydra during World War II. Developed by Skydance Upcoming Media, led by Amy Hennig, it’s been repeatedly delayed, and only cinematic footage has been released. This has understandably caused many to question the game’s fate.

According to recent reports, however, a few hours after the cancellation rumor made the rounds, Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier reported on Bluesky that Skydance’s leadership addressed the rumor with the development team on Slack and assured them Marvel 1943 was not canceled. However, Schreier adds this could change due to the uncertainty caused by the recent merger between Warner Bros. Discovery and Paramount Skydance (Skydance New Media is a game development branch of the now-merged Skydance Corporation).

Skydance Games told the development team behind Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra on Slack this afternoon that the game is not canceled, despite a widely circulated rumor on Twitter today claiming that it was.

Furthermore, Kotaku’s Rebekah Valentine clarified in her report that Marvel 1943 executive producer Lu Giglotti told staff in a Skydance Slack message he’d spoken directly with the executive leadership team to confirm Marvel 1943 is still alive, saying, "There is no truth to these claims." According to Kotaku’s report, Giglotti informed the team that Marvel 1943 was approaching an Alpha milestone later this month. Giglotti also told staff not to let the rumor distract them and that Skydance was "monitoring the situation" to address in the future.

In a recent development, kotaku’s report also sheds light on the game’s tumultuous development cycle. Marvel 1943 was originally pitched as a Netflix game before it was eventually turned into a console and PC title. This transition means the current iteration is “light on gameplay” and lacks substantial interactions, with players primarily using a single button to play it.

It has been revealed that this isn't a completely surprising revelation, as Marvel 1943 was billed as a narrative-driven, linear single-player experience when it was revealed, but the style of game has never been clear. The same reveal also saw Skydance promise the game boasted "intuitive controls and exhilarating second-to-second gameplay that captures the action and excitement of Marvel, inspired by landmark comics, television, and films, as they navigate this all-upcoming globe-trotting adventure." This disconnect may be attributed to Kotaku also reporting that Marvel 1943 is “well over budget,” and its overall scope has been heavily scaled back. Regardless, the outlet’s source claims the game is “close to done.”.

Sources indicate that marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was initially slated to launch in 2025. It was then delayed to early 2026 "to add more polish", according to Skydance, before being pushed again to an undetermined launch window. The game has no announced platforms.

Industry observers note that although Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra appears safe for now, other recent projects have not been as fortunate. Be sure to read our stories about the recent high-profile cancellations of Gang of Dragon and Fairgames.

[Sources: Jason Schreier, Kotaku].

9 Best Tech Parodies in GTA 6

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the Grand Theft Auto series tends to be a parody of real life, with there being loads of satirical comedy woven throughout the many fibers of each game.
  • Tech plays a significant role in the game, as you use your phone for many things, such as ordering a ride on the RydeMe app, or even bucking yourself using the aptly named BuckMe app.
  • You are going to be relying on a lot of tech companies throughout GTA 6, so it is obvious that there will be a number of jokes surrounding them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the Grand Theft Auto series tends to be a parody of real life, with there being loads of satirical comedy woven throughout the many fibers of each game. This trend continues in Grand Theft Auto 6, with there being loads of hilarious parodies of well-known companies, television reveals, radio broadcasts, and even tech.

Tech plays a significant role in the game, as you use your phone for many things, such as ordering a ride on the RydeMe app, or even bucking yourself using the aptly named BuckMe app.

You are going to be relying on a lot of tech companies throughout GTA 6, so it is obvious that there will be a number of jokes surrounding them.

Texting plays a huge role in real life. After all, you text your friends, family members, and even coworkers about what is going on in your life. The same is done in GTA 6, and the game captures texting quite well, with both protagonists texting one another and various people about jobs.

While you may normally use the popular WhatsApp application to get your fill of communication, the people of GTA 6 use a slightly different app called WhatUp. This is a very obvious parody of WhatsApp, with a name that is almost identical.

Even the user interface is almost identical, with it featuring a very minimalist style showing the avatar or profile picture of each contact next to the messages.

Amazon is a go-to tech and shipping company for many people nowadays. While we all may complain about capitalism, there is no denying the convenience of having everything at your fingertips through the use of an app that has next-day shipping.

In GTA, the citizens of Leonida are using a slightly different company that is a clear parody of Amazon, and it is called Sahara. You can find boxes scattered around that mimic the exact shipping tape used by the company, the logo is very similar, and there is even Sahara Mirage, which is meant to be a parody of Amazon Prime.

In a recent development, money makes the world go ‘round in real life, and it especially makes the world go ‘round in GTA 6. You are on a constant mission to collect money in the game, which in a way mimics real life. Anyway when you are handling money in real life, you might use a banking app, or you might use CashApp or Venmo.

GTA 6 has an app that parodies these real-life tools and it is called BuckMe - a hilarious name that has various uses, such as when you give yourself money, which is called bucking yourself.

This app is the go-to banking app that you get at the start of the game because you can’t afford to open a real checking account and it is just perfect.

Sources indicate that did you know that you can play games within GTA 6? Odds are you probably did, and it is thanks to Cal. He so graciously installs the newly introduced JoyStation in Jason’s home early in the game, allowing you to catch up on your gaming within your game.

The JoyStation is an obvious parody of the PlayStation 5, with the console looking almost identical to the real-life system you are probably playing GTA 6 on. Even the user interface looks extremely close to the real-life version.

The console isn’t just for looks, as it can be used to play some real games, with some of them even being easter eggs for real-life movies and games.

In a recent development, when you need to get around the city in real life, you either rely on your car to get you from point A to point B, or you rely on someone else’s car. This can come in the form of a ride that you hire via a rideshare app like Lyft or Uber.

Just like in real life, you can get from point to point in GTA 6 by using the convenient ridesharing app aptly called RydeMe. It even comes complete with a Y instead of an I so you know it was made by the tech bros in Silicon Valley.

The app is great, as it lets you fast travel around the city. If only you could skip the unwanted conversation with the driver in real life. At least the prices match up with the inflated real-life equivalent.

It has been revealed that doomscrolling has become the norm lately, as apps like YouTube, Instagram, and TikTok all offer short-form content that you can easily digest and swipe away. Luckily, GTA 6 hasn’t gone that far… yet.

Sources indicate that while you can’t doomscroll reels in GTA 6, you can flip through tons of posts thanks to the improved Snapmatic app. This app made an appearance in GTA 5, as it was used to take pictures.

In a recent development, now, you can use it to scroll through countless posts about how we got something else before RAC 7. You can even read the comments, and those are something else entirely, so be prepared.

Industry observers note that dating in real life has been boiled down to a few different dating apps, but if you are looking to hook up with someone, you are probably going to use Tinder. Of course, you could try FarmersOnly, but to each their own.

In a recent development, sadly, you can’t get the experience of using a dating app in GTA 6, but you can help out Cal. Early in the game, you get to see the in-game version of Tinder, as Cal hands you his phone and you get to swipe right or left on various dating profiles.

The app is pretty accurate to the real-life equivalent, complete with cringy profiles, horrible pictures, and people with way too high of standards.

According to recent reports, there has been a rise of people who are vaping, and as someone who used to vape all the time, it is sad to see how much it has grown at times. Vaping has infected the world of Leonida as well, but one in particular that is worth pointing out is Manifestick.

This hilarious parody is meant to replace anxiety pens and mock those who wear a vape on a leash around their neck, as there are women who use them like they are addicted to them.

Oh wait, that is because they are addicted. You can discover that these vape pens are laced with cocaine, making them not so friendly and very addictive like the real-life nicotine infused sticks.

Cryptocurrency is everywhere nowadays. There are people who swear on Bitcoin, and we see a meme coin pop up almost every day. We have all heard stories of people being scammed because someone did a rug pull.

Industry observers note that throughout the game, you will interact with a company called AudaCity, and there is even a character named Papa Audacity. This company is creating DacityCoin, and you are meant to promote it with Redbull-style stunts that push the coin’s value up.

The protagonists even call out how the coin is a scam, but that doesn’t mean you can’t get in on the ground floor and be one of the few who profits off of everyone else’s losses.

IBM quantum computer solves problem classical computers can’t in just 15 minutes

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1006 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that an IBM quantum computer has completed an extraordinarily complex computational task in just 15 minutes, while leading methods for simulating the calculation on conventional computers would require prohibitively long runtimes.
  • The achievement, led by IBM and researchers from the University of Chicago, satisfies the fundamental criteria for quantum advantage.
  • In a recent development, in their new paper, "Sampling hard circuits with verifiably high fidelity," the researchers demonstrated that both objectives could be achieved simultaneously using a novel design for encoded quantum circuits.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that an IBM quantum computer has completed an extraordinarily complex computational task in just 15 minutes, while leading methods for simulating the calculation on conventional computers would require prohibitively long runtimes. Perhaps even more significantly, researchers were able to establish statistical confidence in the accuracy of the quantum computer's results, addressing one of the biggest obstacles in the field.

The achievement, led by IBM and researchers from the University of Chicago, satisfies the fundamental criteria for quantum advantage. This milestone occurs when a quantum computer performs a computational task beyond the practical capabilities of leading classical computing methods while producing results that can be trusted.

In a recent development, in their new paper, "Sampling hard circuits with verifiably high fidelity," the researchers demonstrated that both objectives could be achieved simultaneously using a novel design for encoded quantum circuits. The experiment represents one of the largest demonstrations of logical quantum computing to date. The researchers have also made their circuits and experimental results publicly available through the Quantum Advantage Tracker.

Solving Quantum Computing's Verification Problem.

Unlike conventional computers, which process information using bits that represent either zero or one, quantum computers rely on quantum bits, or qubits. These can exist in combinations of both states and interact through a phenomenon known as quantum entanglement. These properties allow quantum computers to approach certain computational problems in fundamentally different ways.

For years, scientists have tested the capabilities of quantum computers using a benchmark called random circuit sampling (RCS). This technique involves running a series of randomly selected quantum operations and generating samples from a complex probability distribution. As the circuits grow larger and more complicated, reproducing their output with a classical computer becomes increasingly difficult.

Industry observers note that however, this approach creates a fundamental dilemma. If a computation is too difficult for a classical computer to reproduce, how can researchers establish that the quantum computer performed it correctly?

As computational complexity increases, independently verifying the results becomes progressively more difficult and eventually impractical without making strong assumptions about how accurately the quantum hardware operates.

In a recent development, to overcome this problem, the IBM and University of Chicago team developed a more structured alternative to random circuit sampling. The researchers mathematically demonstrated that their approach preserves the same computational hardness criteria as conventional RCS while introducing a structure that allows errors to be detected during the computation.

It has been revealed that "Verification remains one of the biggest challenges in firmly establishing experimental quantum advantage," said Bill Fefferman, Associate Professor at the University of Chicago. "This experiment develops techniques to better characterize the fidelity of hard quantum states under noise, increasing confidence that the quantum computer is solving a computationally hard problem.".

Soumik Ghosh, PhD student in Fefferman's group at the University of Chicago, added, "Beyond strengthening experimental validation, advances in verification have the potential to unlock practical applications for the next generation of quantum computers.".

70 Logical Qubits and Tenfold Lower Error Rates.

One of the greatest challenges in building powerful quantum computers is their extraordinary sensitivity to errors. Quantum information can be disrupted by environmental disturbances, imperfections in hardware, and inaccuracies in the operations used to manipulate qubits. As computations become longer and more complex, these errors can accumulate and undermine the reliability of the results.

Sources indicate that quantum error correction addresses this weakness by encoding quantum information across multiple physical qubits to create more reliable units known as logical qubits. This approach allows certain errors to be identified and, depending on the technique, corrected or accounted for without destroying the underlying quantum information.

According to recent reports, in one of the largest known demonstrations of quantum error correction, the researchers performed computations using 70 protected logical qubits. The experiment involved 2,415 logical two-qubit operations and 468 logical "T gates.".

In a recent development, quantum gates are the fundamental operations that manipulate quantum information, much like logic gates in conventional computers. Two-qubit gates allow qubits to interact, while T gates enable additional types of quantum operations needed for universal quantum computing. Together, these gate counts illustrate the considerable complexity of the experiment.

Recent findings suggest that by encoding the quantum circuits, the researchers achieved effective logical error rates 10 times lower than the underlying physical error rates. This substantial reduction allowed the quantum computer to maintain remarkably high fidelity, a measure of how closely the actual quantum state matches the intended one, despite performing thousands of complex operations.

It has been revealed that "We are now firmly in the quantum advantage era," said Jay Gambetta, Director of IBM Research and IBM Fellow. "We have demonstrated a quantum computation beyond the practical reach of classical computers that establishes, with statistical confidence, a lower bound on how faithfully it was executed. This milestone gives scientists, developers, and businesses a newly introduced foundation for trusting quantum computers as they scale to problems far beyond what we can achieve classically.".

The researchers found that many leading classical simulation techniques would require impractically long periods to reproduce the computation. IBM's quantum computer, by comparison, accomplished the task in approximately 15 minutes.

Although the experiment was designed to demonstrate quantum advantage rather than solve an immediate real-world problem, it addresses two essential requirements for making large-scale quantum computing practical: controlling errors and establishing confidence in computational results.

By demonstrating both capabilities in a computation beyond the practical reach of leading classical methods, the researchers have taken a significant step toward a future in which quantum computers could reliably tackle scientific and industrial problems that are right now out of reach.

After a one-month delay, we’re finally days away now from the start of Battlefield 6’s Season 2 of live service. The second season is being revealed today, following weeks of teasers, and some Battlefield Labs testing of the first latest map arriving with the new season.

It’s all going to kick off with a gameplay reveal, which is set to stream live later today.

As we’ve come to expect, the Season 2 reveal will take place via a YouTube premiere. It’s set to kick off live at 8am PT, 11am ET, 4pm GMT on the official Battlefield channel on YouTube - and embedded below. Today’s reveal will also be followed by a more detailed roadmap of Season 2, which will give us a much better idea about the volume and cadence of content we can expect.

In a recent development, season 2 goes live February 17, kicking off a new chapter in the continued conflict between NATO and Pax Armata. The medium-large new map, Contaminated, will be available immediately at the season’s launch. Contaminated takes placed in the mountains of Germany, centered around a once NATO-owned airbase.

VL-7 psychoactive smoke appears to factor majorly into the gameplay of this upcoming season, though we’re waiting to hear more details on that. We can expect new weapons, new gadgets, and the awaited return of the AH-6 Little Bird helicopter.

Look forward to more coverage from us as more details are revealed later today.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that fnatic has made its first confirmed exit official as it rebuilds its LEC roster for 2027.
  • The club marked the departure with a farewell video titled “Thank You, Iván”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that fnatic has confirmed the departure of its longest-serving player, jungler Razork, who is set to join Team Heretics. With support Lospa also set to leave, the London club faces a near-total LEC roster rebuild for 2027.

Sources indicate that fnatic has made its first confirmed exit official as it rebuilds its LEC roster for 2027. Razork was the London club’s longest-serving player and its main playmaker. He leaves after five seasons in the jungle.

The club marked the departure with a farewell video titled “Thank You, Iván”. In it, Fnatic recalls him arriving as a young player with huge ambition. He had entered the LEC with Misfits Gaming in 2020 before moving to Fnatic in 2022. The club later extended his contract to run through 2026.

According to recent reports, his next stop appears to be Team Heretics. Sheep Esports reported that the 26-year-old will play alongside midlaner Jackies and support Jun. Heretics had already tried to sign him a year earlier. On that occasion it agreed a buyout with Fnatic but could not agree terms with the player.

The rebuild runs deeper than the jungle. Every Fnatic team member except Lospa was due out of contract in 2026. The support was signed until the end of 2027.

Recent findings suggest that that deal will not keep him at Fnatic either. Lospa has reportedly agreed verbally to join SK Gaming for 2027. No buyout is involved in moving his contract between the two clubs. With that move, the one contract running beyond 2026 also leaves the club.

In the jungle, Yike is set to replace Razork in a 2027 line-up of Soboro, Yike, Vladi, Doggo and Labrov, according to Sheep Esports sources.

Sources indicate that the overhaul follows a difficult year. Fnatic finished eighth in LEC 2026 Versus. It then placed seventh in Spring, which ended on 10 May. Summer brought the same finishing position.

A loss to GIANTX on 30 August kept the team out of the Summer playoffs. That defeat left the club absent from Worlds for the first time since 2016.

In a recent development, 5 years of memories. it was an honour to see you grow into the person and player you are 🧡 https://t.co/F3TWY9WZqq pic.twitter.com/K3K3EQICZ1.

— FNATIC (@FNATIC) November 17, 2026.

It has been revealed that for the UK scene, the scale of change matters. Fnatic is one of the LEC’s best-supported clubs among British fans.

The club has also opened a search for a League of Legends General Manager. Its job advert notes Fnatic goes into a rebuild in 2027. The latest hire will run recruitment of players, coaches and staff, including transfers and benchings, and will manage the team’s budget.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Xbox have confirmed that Wolfenstein 3 is indeed in production at Indiana Jones and the Great Circle devs MachineGames and that Doom makers id Software have started work on their next game after losing a bunch of staff to the mass layoffs across Microsoft's gaming division this year.
  • According to recent reports, "A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations," isn't part of the marketing spiel for either of those games.
  • The Wolfenstein and id confirmations came as Xbox had a bit of a social media party to commemorate their 25th birthday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xbox have confirmed that Wolfenstein 3 is indeed in production at Indiana Jones and the Great Circle devs MachineGames and that Doom makers id Software have started work on their next game after losing a bunch of staff to the mass layoffs across Microsoft's gaming division this year.

According to recent reports, "A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations," isn't part of the marketing spiel for either of those games. Instead, it's something Xbox CEO Asha Shama has bellowed amid a rant outlining how she sees the company's future.

The Wolfenstein and id confirmations came as Xbox had a bit of a social media party to commemorate their 25th birthday. Sharma, ever keen to be seen right next to any positive news coming out of the firm, confirmed Wolfenstein 3 is in production by posting a photo showing a few lines from its script. Around the same time, she shouted out Doom: The Dark Ages Revelations' incoming Slaughter Mode, adding that "the team is already working on its next game".

The official id Software account responded to note that this next game is being made by their "teams in Texas and Frankfurt, with game direction once again by Hugo Martin", and that "it'll be some time before [they're] ready to share more".

We're incredibly excited about our next project, a new game from our teams in Texas and Frankfurt, with game direction once again by Hugo Martin. It'll be some time before we're ready to share more but we can't wait for you to see what we're working on.

Alongside hollering about these couple of games, Sharma put out a 25th anniversary statement which for the most part does the sort of bigging up of Xbox's past you'd expect. Good times were had, we blazed a trail and made lots of money, etcetera. The final section saw the exec attempt to look forward to the next 25 years for Xbox.

It has been revealed that "While modern games demonstrate the heights of human craft in ways unimaginable just decades ago, the cost, resources, and risk required to create them have grown just as dramatically," she wrote. "As a result, too many ideas never become games, and too many games fall short of what their creators imagined. For decades, this has been the unavoidable tradeoff of ambition. We must change this.

Sources indicate that "Throughout human history, the scale of what we could create was determined by the people, capital, and resources we could command. That relationship is beginning to break. A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations. A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars. And our largest studios will be able to pursue ambitions as far beyond today's games as Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is from its first entry in 1982.".

That certainly sounds a lot like the sales pitch the biggest proponents of generative AI keep wheeling out, while avoiding saying generative AI out loud in the hopes of making it more palatable to folks who might not make the connection. I'm waiting for Sharma to put out another post revealing that she accidentally mixed another section of the Wolfenstein script into her celebratory musings, but I'm not holding my breath.

Xbox parent company Microsoft are still at the moment subject to a BDS movement boycott over their reported ties to the Israeli military.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nioh 3 has received a hot newly introduced update that brings plenty of bug fixes to very specific concerns, but it also implements fixes for a few of the most common - and incredibly annoying - bugs. Patch 1.03.01 arrived earlier on all platforms, and it comes with a chunky set of notes.

This latest update, predictably, doesn’t add any gameplay features, but some of the included fixes will absolutely delight - or vindicate - so many of the game’s millions of players.

There’s plenty to go through in the patch notes published today for enhancement 1.03.01, but the most impactful is a fix for an concern that “sometimes made it impossible to use elixirs during battle.” This is only a partial fix, but if you ran into the problem of smashing that shortcut button and not seeing your character play the healing animation, you’ll be glad to see it.

Sources indicate that this is a problem myself and others have faced, especially in boss fights. You can even see the shortcut register your button press and proceed to ignore you. Another partial fix has been made to an issue that caused the game to crash. Team Ninja didn’t share specifics on that, and though Nioh 3 has been fairly stable for me in 70+ hours, it has definitely crashed a few times.

If you’ve been playing since launch, you likely have - or know someone who has - run into issues with save file corruption and other weird bugs around certain trackable items within save files.

Team Ninja already rolled out a couple of fixes there, and this latest one specifically targets losing valuables during Myths. If your save file has been affected, the game will now check and recover what was lost. Even more interesting is that the game will now automatically create a backup copy of your save data any time you load a save.

If you’ve made it into the Eternal Rift, you’ll be happy to know that today’s patch takes care of a few progression blockers, and fixes an concern that allowed some players to obtain certain items before they were supposed to, locking themselves out.

One of the more amusing fixes concerns Mujina, who had a tendency to respawn if you prayed at a Shrine after opening a chest it was hiding in, which made it appear far more often than a mimic should.

Finally, there’s a set of fixes that address bugs (and exploits) when using specific Martial Art with certain weapons. There are a few fixes to AI, Myths, and one problem with the Minamoto no Yoritomo boss fight that made it impossible to interrupt him, even after he runs out of Ki.

Sources indicate that hit the link at the top for the full change log, and check out our Nioh 3 gameplay tips if you haven’t already. You should also change these settings ASAP, as they’re going to make your life much easier and save you a lot of time.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, in development for years, and running on a custom C++ engine, Horu is inspired by 2006 hybrid RTS Star Wars: Empire at War - good, not great, in the words of turncoat jankonaut Graham, and the subject of many mods.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Clicking a random link this morning, I was dazzled by the glare of a thousand laser batteries firing simultaneously. My ears trembled beneath the trundle of a million caterpillar tracks. Balls of ice, bolts of lightning, shipments of rare alloys, and cascades of drop pods went screaming down my nerves and detonated in my frontal cortex, painting starlanes across the inside of my skull. "Oh god, they've finally found us!" I yelled, hiding beneath my desk. "I for one welcome our upcoming galactic overlords!".

It has been revealed that but then I realised that I wasn't looking at a live newsfeed, but merely the Steam page for Horu, a real-time 4X strategy game in which you can "command hundreds of thousands of units across land and space", in the summary of developer David "GlassBeaver" Nadaski. There's also a magic system, this being "the spice that makes your enemy's defeat bitter", which is a very genteel way to characterise glaciating a tank formation or conjuring a miniature blackhole.

In a recent development, in development for years, and running on a custom C++ engine, Horu is inspired by 2006 hybrid RTS Star Wars: Empire at War - good, not great, in the words of turncoat jankonaut Graham, and the subject of many mods. Horu's way of bettering Empire at War is seemingly to add a shedload more of everything. You can engage in a fleet battle that looks like two migrating ant hives colliding, even as a frankly unnecessary quantity of cyborgs pour over the forgeworld beneath and get their shit kicked in by some tornado-summoning sorcerers.

Sources indicate that offensives appear to work like this: any drop ships that push through the fleet battle add meat to the ground invasion, with the option of deploying wormholes to sneak your troops behind the defending armada. On the ground, you're basically out to capture control points. You're allegedly spared from "continuous babysitting" by semi-autonomous squadron commanders and an orders system that lets you queue up objectives, before units engage in battle.

In a recent development, you can still give individual orders to units, but that seems like a recipe for acute wrist injury. There's also a boarding action mechanic whereby your hijackers move through vessels room by room. Again, I struggle to understand how you'll have time and dexterity to oversee such skulduggery when there are a bajillion particle cannons going off all at once.

Outside of combat, there are planets to develop, shipyards to build, spy networks to groom, research trees to water, and stock markets to manipulate. It all looks like business as usual for an imperial 4X. Honestly, I can imagine the maximalist warfaring being a hot mess, and then there's the fact that the dev is running a Kickstarter "to fund the remaining assets needed for a playable build: more spaceships, more units, more animations, more sounds, more music, and everything in between." I've been burned by Kickstarter overpromising before. Still, I can only admire the vindictive intellect that would have me play a little game of FTL inside what looks like one of the larger PvP scraps from Eve Online.

You can read more on Steam. Release date there is presently none. For an equally populous strategy experience that's closer in style to Supreme Commander, check out Sanctuary: Shattered Space.

In a recent development, nongshim RedForce have brought 2022 world champion Deft back to the LCK and paired him again with Kingen and Pyosik. The move follows an eighth-place 2026 for the club and comes days after BLG ended Korea's four-year hold on the World Championship.

Kim ‘Deft’ Hyuk-kyu’s signing was confirmed on 19 November. The club used its official social media channels to make the announcement. Deft began his military service after the 2024 season ended.

The deal reunites him with two members of the DRX side that won the 2022 World Championship. Jungler Hong ‘Pyosik’ Chang-hyeon joined later the same day, alongside support Moon ‘Andil’ Gwan-bin. Top laner Hwang ‘Kingen’ Seong-hoon had re-signed a day earlier.

Industry observers note that deft’s signing was announced at 7pm. The Pyosik and Andil additions that followed completed Nongshim’s five-man starting line-up, Inven Global reported. Mid laner Seon ‘Calix’ Hyeon-bin provides continuity. He has been with the organisation since 2021 and extended his deal on 18 November.

Deft brings a long winning record. He made his debut with MVP Blue in 2013. His titles include the LCK, the LPL, the Mid-Season Invitational and the 2022 World Championship.

Kingen first joined Nongshim for the 2025 season. Pyosik arrives after a difficult 2026 at DN SOOPers. That team lost a run of matches, and rookie Sharvel took his starting place.

Industry observers note that the move had been signalled. About a month before the announcement, Sheep Esports reported from Korean sources that Nongshim planned to sign Deft. The same report remarked rookie AD carry Diable would need a fresh team.

Industry observers note that the signings mark a sharp change of direction after a poor year. Once the league campaign was over, the team lasted just a single match in the play-ins.

Industry observers note that the deal lands days after a setback for the whole league. Bilibili Gaming’s victory over Gen.G came at the Barclays Center in New York. It gave the organisation its first Summoner’s Cup.

BLG won all four of its series against LCK teams at the tournament. Every LCK seed fell to the Chinese side on its way to the trophy. The title is also the LPL’s first since EDward Gaming won in 2021.

'Deft' has signed a contract as the upcoming ADC of NS RedForce LCK Team.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The latest significant content update has been revealed for HoYoverse's breakout game, Genshin Impact. Version Luna 5, which has the unusually long and needlessly layered title — Song of the Welkin Moon: Variation - Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind — is set to arrive February 25.

In a recent development, this one is a bit of a nostalgia play, taking everyone back to Mondstadt, the place where you may remember taking your first steps. And, as with any good return to the ol’ hunting grounds, come familiar characters, too.

The substantial latest arrival is Varka, who joins as a playable character for the first time. Varka, Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius, is a character whose debut has been long-awaited. He is a 5-Star Anemo Claymore wielder with a dual-wield combat style, capable of dealing two different types of Elemental damage. His addition means that there's now finally a burly 5-Star male character of each elemental type... do with that information what you will.

In a recent development, varka's dual-wielding combat style allows him to deal two different types of Elemental damage at the same time. The way it works is that his Elemental Skill boosts the damage of his regular attacks, but it also converts the damage type of his right-hand claymore to match his teammates’ elements (Pyro, Hydro, Electro, or Cryo). The left-hand claymore always deals Anemo damage.

According to recent reports, the more normal attacks you use, the more frequently he can activate a special Elemental Skill, or trigger a Charged Attack that doesn’t consume stamina. He can also rely on the Hexerei effect to trigger more instances of Elemental Skill, as well as Charged Attacks, making him a monster damage-dealer.

According to recent reports, varka, of course, has been a staple member of the cast, featuring in both the original story in a small cameo, as well as taking a bigger role in the recent Nod-Krai chapters. With the return to Mondstadt, his playable debut makes sense. His Story Quest will shed light on his encounter with the Wild Hunt, and the Great Wolf King of the North.

The reruns for this version are going to be Flins — who will be available in the first phase of Event Wishes — as well as Skirk and Escoffier in the second phase. You can also look forward to the return of the Chronicled Wish with Mondstadt characters.

Staying on the theme of reminiscence, the significant event in Luna 5 is centered around revisiting memories from the beginning of your time with Genshin Impact, and reuniting with old friends. In Echoes of Memory, you’ll witness familiar scenes that have been changed slightly, and you’ll need to use the Spotter Kamera to detect and record those differences.

The Knights of Favonius are hosting several other activities for everyone to take part in, including an event that lets you catch up with old friends over drinks which you make for them.

Outside of events, there’s a latest set of Gliding and Combat Challenges. And, of course, there are new minigames that you can relax with. The Kamera is being utilised yet again, and this time you can use to capture sights from your time in spots across Natlan, Fontaine, and Sumeru. There’s also… a horde mode of a sort, where you fend off waves of enemies.

Catch up on the latest set of Genshin Impact codes before you play, and check out why we think Genshin Impact is one of the best mobile games you can play today.

CD Projekt Red CEO Puts Ambition Ahead of Budget in Witcher and Cyberpunk Development

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (674 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s no secret that Grand Theft Auto 6 was not a cheap game to make, to put very, very mildly.
  • According to recent reports, considering the amount of cash that undoubtedly went into GTA 6’s development, which has now been followed by immense success and landmark profits for Rockstar and Take-Two, also in the billions, something of a new precedent has been established for the AAA gaming sector.
  • It has been revealed that obviously, this is completely untrue, but that doesn’t stop people from wondering, especially as far as other power-player devs are concerned.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s no secret that Grand Theft Auto 6 was not a cheap game to make, to put very, very mildly. While Rockstar has not publicly disclosed the game’s precise internal price tag, rumors have circulated that it’s somewhere in the billions, and considering the sheer scope and complexity of the game’s world, I don’t think that theory is an unreasonable one.

According to recent reports, considering the amount of cash that undoubtedly went into GTA 6’s development, which has now been followed by immense success and landmark profits for Rockstar and Take-Two, also in the billions, something of a new precedent has been established for the AAA gaming sector. Arguably, it's not a great one: if you keep pouring massive stacks of cash into your game, it’ll magically make billions of dollars forever.

It has been revealed that obviously, this is completely untrue, but that doesn’t stop people from wondering, especially as far as other power-player devs are concerned. For example, CD Projekt Red, developer and publisher of landmark IPs like The Witcher and Cyberpunk, has invested its fair share of capital into its works. However, according to its CEO, Michal Nowakowski, the budget of CDPR’s titles is secondary to their ambitions and goals.

During CD Projekt Red’s Q3 2026 Earnings Call, the audio of which was posted to the manufacturer’s official YouTube channel, Nowakowski was asked his opinion on the “technological and qualitative leap” between Grand Theft Auto 5 and 6, and in turn, how those landmark advancements might inform CDPR’s developmental philosophy going forward, particularly with in-development Witcher and Cyberpunk titles.

Nowakowski acknowledged the major precedent that has been put forth by Rockstar through GTA 6 through the industry at large, but he also clarified that, in spite of that game’s success, he and his company don’t make their games just to compete with those produced by another.

In a recent development, “If anything happened as a result of GTA 6, it's always great to see games like that because they show you how much cool stuff can be done. That's for sure an inspiration in many ways for our developers.”.

He and his firm don’t make their games just to compete with those produced by another.

When asked how GTA 6’s developmental scope might affect budget expectations for upcoming games, Nowakowski stressed that Witcher and Cyberpunk are not “budget-driven developments,” and while he is always conscious of how much money it costs to make top-shelf games, it’s not really conducive to a product’s health to be constantly keeping the budget in mind during the developmental process.

“They are ambition-driven developments and money is notable, the budgets are not indefinite, that's not what we're saying. And honestly, that philosophy has not changed for us because of GTA 6.”.

The obvious problem with expecting new games, even AAA ones, to have comparable budget and scope to GTA 6 is that not every game is GTA 6, nor is every developer Rockstar. Not everyone is going to have that kind of raw spending power available, and certainly, not everyone has access to the kind of prestige IP with a baked-in fanbase like GTA.

According to recent reports, overbloated budgets for AAA games have already been a consistent problem and talking point for at least a decade now, with players regularly complaining that too much money is spent on making games look visually and technologically impressive without making the core experience any better. This ends up dragging out development cycles and bleeding companies dry, not to mention subjecting developmental staff to intense crunch. Heck, lest we forget, GTA 6 took over a decade itself to come out, and was delayed twice.

Recent findings suggest that while it is heartening to hear Nowakowski’s proclamation of ambition over budget, it is very difficult to predict where the AAA sector is going now that the shadow of GTA 6 is looming over it. Personally, I’d like to believe that players won’t expect every upcoming game they play to also be GTA 6-tier, but, well….

Sources indicate that with a name like Lootbox RPG, it's not hard to see developer Mario Gaida's turn-based dungeon crawler is a bit of a snapshot of 2019, back when lootboxes were all the rage. But, while lootboxes have gone the way of the DoDo, Lootbox RPG is still going strong with its largest update yet that comes absolutely jam-packed with content!

Industry observers note that I really do mean largest too. Just for a taster, the 2.0 revision for Lootbox RPG includes five new regions to explore, including an icy spire and sweltering desert pyramid, alongside a host of new bosses to face in these areas. You can now reach up to level 60 and gear level 70, offering even more opportunities for insane levels of power.

Again, it's interesting to see Lootbox RPG, a dungeon crawler at least partially built around parodying some elements of what, at the time, were an infamous part of gaming, suddenly embrace fresh trends such as base building. That's not to say it's a bad thing, but definitely interesting to note.

Either way, Lootbox RPG's 2.0 update, available now, includes a whole host of newly introduced additions. All of this is built on an RPG that already has hours' worth of content to explore. So if you were interested, you can find Lootbox RPG available to play on iOS and Android today!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that microsoft 365 isn't quite living up to its name this week, as its services have suffered an extended outage that's knocked the likes of Outlook, Teams, and Copilot for six. As of writing, the organization are finally reporting "encouraging recovery progress in Europe" and are busy "addressing the remaining areas of disruption", but that's only after chunks of November 12th and 13th have seen people, businesses, and institutions left unable to use stuff they rely on.

Recent findings suggest that that latest update was given by Microsoft to the BBC, who've had a live report on the outage running, since it's affected the likes of schools, government services and medical services. IGN and Kotaku's reports differ on whether any Xbox services appear to be affected. The Xbox status support page currently indicates all is swell, but Downdetector does show a recent uptick in reports of challenges.

It has been revealed that "We regret that today’s outages caused disruptions for our customers, and we are working to address the glitch," Microsoft exec Charles LaManna wrote in response to a support thread on the topic in the early hours of November 13th UK time. "We will continue to share more information as soon as we have it, and for now I can confirm that there is no indication this is the result of malicious or cyber activity.".

As much as it's slightly reassuring that there currently looks to have been no big hack, the time it's taken to deploy proper fixes is concerning, with Microsoft noting some of their early attempts at rectifying things "not taking as expected".

The debacle has rather emphasised how far from ideal it is that so much key infrastructure across the world runs on one clump of tech which all go down in a heartbeat, but to a certain degree that is the peril of relying on anything. One can only hope that Microsoft's ongoing efforts to fire vast numbers of staff into the sun and embrace AI haven't factored into lots of their services going tits up for an inconvenient amount of time.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, even before the game came out, it was pretty easy to guess that Nioh 3 would be a hit. From the word of mouth leading up to launch, to the well-received free demo, there was little chance the action RPG wasn’t going to be a major deal.

Today, publisher Koei Tecmo has announced that the game has officially passed over one million copies sold worldwide across PC, and PlayStation 5. This makes it the fastest in the Nioh franchise to reach this milestone.

Sources indicate that as a result of this fantastic launch, Nioh 3 has now pushed overall Nioh franchise sales to be over 10 million, which includes the original Nioh as well as Nioh 2. Today’s news comes just two weeks after the game arrived on PC, and PS5.

On Steam, where it’s available on PC, it shot up the Steam charts, and immediately broke the series’ previous best peak concurrent player count record. From there, the numbers kept growing, leading up to a stellar weekend where it peaked at 88,045 concurrent players on Steam, double that of its launch day.

This now stands as the largest for any Nioh game on Steam, and though we don’t have insight into how well it’s doing on PS5 specifically, it still highlights that the Nioh series continues to grow.

Nioh 3 builds on everything the two prior games established, and pushes the series into the semi-open-world realm, with several larger maps that each cover a period of time in Japan’s history. In our Nioh 3 review we called it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.”.

If you’re curious about the challenging and very rewarding action RPG, start with these gameplay tips, and don’t be shy to call upon a friend (or stranger) for help using our co-op guide.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • We all know the story of GTA 5 making more than $1 billion in the first three days it was on sale, right?
  • It has been revealed that at least, that's according to one analyst, Joost van Dreunen, a senior data analyst and great writer/numbers diviner who wrote some predictions in his respected SuperJoost PlayList newsletter.
  • Let's review what we already know: there is a conservative estimate of 10 million pre-orders for Rockstar's latest game floating around - something buoyed by comments from Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick - and, even by the firm's lofty expectations, we know the game is tracking "well above expectations" when it comes to pre-orders.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We all know the story of GTA 5 making more than $1 billion in the first three days it was on sale, right? At the time, Take-Two believed this to be the fastest any entertainment property had achieved the impressive milestone - music and films included. It made history, and with ease. And it looks like GTA 6 is going to do even better.

It has been revealed that at least, that's according to one analyst, Joost van Dreunen, a senior data analyst and great writer/numbers diviner who wrote some predictions in his respected SuperJoost PlayList newsletter. "My prediction: Take-Two reveals opening-weekend sales above $2 billion by Monday, 23rd November," he wrote. And you know what? I reckon he's onto something.

Let's review what we already know: there is a conservative estimate of 10 million pre-orders for Rockstar's latest game floating around - something buoyed by comments from Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick - and, even by the firm's lofty expectations, we know the game is tracking "well above expectations" when it comes to pre-orders.

Recent findings suggest that we also know a lot of people are shelling out for the slightly more pricey Ultimate Edition (£90). So many people are opting for the more expensive version, in fact, that Take-Two revised its financial forecast up to $3.5bn for the next financial quarter, thanks to "recurrent consumer spending" (something Zelnick clarified in an investor's call is explicitly linked to the Ultimate Edition). 10 million pre-orders, at roughly $100 per copy - that's $1 billion right off the bat.

Industry observers note that "That’s two days faster than its predecessor," van Dreunen said, "and largely before anyone has even played the game." That other $1bn will come over the weekend. And then, per the analyst, the game will sell roughly another 28 million copies over the course of the first year it's on sale. "My forecast puts first-year sales at 38 million copies, only modestly ahead of GTA 5’s 35 million. The real difference may be how much revenue each player generates over the years that follow.".

According to recent reports, but it's what follows in the newsletter that intrigues me most. "At the high end, [GTA 6] may just lift the entire industry with it," wrote van Dreunen. "In the face of AI slop and shitty mobile games that exist only to extract revenue, it will offer a reprieve. At a time when the industry is increasingly focused on making games cheaper and monetising players more aggressively, Rockstar is about to demonstrate the enduring appeal of spending a fortune to make something people actually want to play.".

So, even if you're dubious about the game and Rockstar's motivations for selling as many copies as possible, the launch of GTA 6 could be something that gives the industry a much-needed jolt of life, in the face of rampant layoffs and shrinking talent pools.

Recent findings suggest that it's not all sunshine and rainbows ahead for Rockstar, though: amongst the frenzy of launch activity, Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees. The case's conclusion will be determined this week, as the game goes on sale.
